title: Deployment Gating Engine: multi-mode traffic shaping and rollback policies
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a reusable Deployment Gating Engine that expresses canary, A/B, and shadow policies consistently across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments while encoding environment-specific constraints (networking, capacity, RBAC, KMS).

Context: Current rollout primitives are fragmented: hosted rollouts use API-layer traffic-splitting; dedicated uses pool-level routing with capacity reservations; private deployments rely on customer-controlled ingress and lack first-class autoscale/rollback integration. Teams need a single declarative model for experiments and safety with deterministic fallback behavior.

Scope (MVP):
- Declarative policy spec that supports: percentage canaries, weighted A/B splits, shadow mirroring (full/partial), staged promotion windows, and automatic rollback triggers (error rate, latency, quality regression).
- Pluggable environment constraint checks: capacity budget, region affinity, KMS/secret access verification, SSO/RBAC guardrails.
- Executor adapters for Hosted (control plane routing + model variant mapping), Dedicated (pool selector + admission control), and Private (sidecar + ingress annotations).
- Observability hooks: per-policy metrics, token-level cost estimation, and automatic incident annotations for rollbacks.

Non-goals (MVP):
- Replacing per-tenant custom runbooks; we aim to provide safe defaults and guardrails.
- Full UI surface for composing policies (Console work planned in follow-up).

Success criteria:
- A single policy YAML can be applied to a model version and produces equivalent traffic behavior in hosted and dedicated test clusters (e2e smoke).
- Auto-rollback triggers fire in a synthetic failure test and rollback completes within SLA.
- No config drift: parity checks catch unsupported config in Private with clear validation errors.

Design notes / trade-offs: 
- Strong consistency vs latency: In Hosted we can centralize routing decisions; in Dedicated/Private we prefer local admission control to reduce cross-network chattiness. Solution: hybrid model — compile high-level policy into environment-appropriate artifacts (control-plane routing for Hosted, local admission policies for Dedicated/Private).
- Security: Private deployments may not allow control plane configuration changes. We will provide a signed artifact bundle customers can apply; artifact contains policy + validation checks and optional operators/sidecars for enforcement.
- Capacity awareness: For Dedicated, policy engine must consult reserved capacity and autoscale buffers. For Hosted, we simulate allocation using capacity forecasts + reserve tokens.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Policy schema v1 (2 sprints): YAML schema + parser, unit tests, and examples for canary/AB/shadow.
2) Hosted executor (3 sprints): integrate with routing service, implement rollout monitor and auto-rollback runner.
3) Dedicated executor (3 sprints): admission controller, pool-aware weighting engine, and capacity predicates.
4) Private artifacts (2 sprints): signed bundles, sidecar validator, and docs for operator apply.
5) Observability and regression harness (2 sprints): metrics + synthetic test suite for rollback validation.

Acceptance criteria for PR: schema validated by regen tests; demo deployment across hosted sandbox and dedicated dev pool with matching behavior; synthetic failure causes auto-rollback and produces annotated timeline in Console logs.

Links and artifacts:
- Design brief: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/DEPL-GATING-DOC (internal design doc)
- Prototype PR (routing): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7842
- Synthetic harness: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/synthetic/rollout-sim

Risks & mitigations: 
- Private env heterogeneity: maintain a conservative validation mode that forbids risky operations and presents explicit manual steps for operator to approve.
- Cross-mode semantic gaps: include a compatibility matrix in schema with clear fallbacks (e.g., shadow sampling not supported in air-gapped on-prem; we provide an agent-based mirror instead).

Open questions: 
- Should A/B experiments expose percentage-by-customer segmentation (per-tenant feature flags) or rely on deterministic hashing? (Tentative: support both; default to deterministic hashing to reduce state).
- How to surface partial enforcement failures in Private without noisy false positives? (Add a suppression window + operator annotation API).

Next steps (short term):
- Tech spec review with Runtime and Infra (scheduled 2026-02-26) — leads: Maya, Luca, Priya.
- Implement schema and unit tests (ENG team spike).
- Coordinate with Console PM to backlog policy authoring UX after v1.

acceptance_criteria: Single policy YAML produces equivalent routing in hosted and dedicated testbeds
Auto-rollback completes within defined SLA during synthetic failure
Policy validation surfaces unsupported config in Private with clear remediation steps
Console timeline annotated and linkable to rollback events
implementation_notes: Compiler will translate high-level policy to three artifact types: control-plane routing rules (hosted), admission config and pool weights (dedicated), signed bundle (private). Executors must expose a status API for Console to poll. Use existing rollout-monitor library for metrics and decision logic.
